question: A 35-year-old G0P1 female presents to her OB/GYN after 17 weeks gestation. A quad screen is performed revealing the following results: elevated inhibin and beta HCG, decreased aFP and estriol. An ultrasound was performed demonstrating increased nuchal translucency. When the fetus is born, what may be some common characteristics of the newborn if amniocentesis confirms the quad test results?

options.opa: Epicanthal folds, high-pitched crying/mewing, and microcephaly
options.opb: Rocker-bottom feet, micrognathia, clenched hands with overlapping finger, and prominent occiput
options.opc: Microphthalmia, microcephaly, cleft lip/palate, holoprosencephaly, and polydactyly
options.opd: Epicanthal folds, macroglossia, flat profile, depressed nasal bridge, and simian palmar crease
options.ope: Elfin facies, low nasal bridge, and extreme friendliness with strangers

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Elevated inhibin and beta HCG -> increased risk of Down syndrome -> 80%
CHAIN: Decreased aFP and estriol -> increased risk of neural tube defects -> 70%
CHAIN: Increased nuchal translucency on ultrasound -> increased risk of chromosomal abnormalities -> 75%
CHAIN: Confirmation of quad screen results by amniocentesis -> increased likelihood of genetic abnormalities -> 85%
analysis: The quad screen results along with the ultrasound findings suggest a high likelihood of a chromosomal abnormality, specifically Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome). The common characteristics associated with Down syndrome include epicanthal folds, high-pitched crying/mewing, microcephaly, and developmental delays.
